statusPolicy: Only publish verified public status. No metrics, milestones, or external destinations without evidence.

products.name: Xondry.com
products.summary: A public portfolio and discovery platform where AI creators publish projects and visitors explore work, creator profiles, challenges, and leaderboards.
products.problem: AI creators need a focused place to present their work and be discovered beyond general-purpose social feeds.
products.audience: AI creators and builders sharing work, plus people looking for new AI-made projects.
products.role: Founder; product direction, discovery model, experience design, and AI-assisted iteration.
decisions: Project pages connect each piece of work to its creator
Explore, challenges, leaderboard, and creator-profile paths
XP and reputation signals for community participation
proof: The public website was reachable on November 2, 2026.
Public navigation exposes Explore, Challenges, Leaderboard, Creators, and profiles.
limitations: Displayed community counts and commercial traction have not been independently audited.
Public content may include illustrative or seeded entries.

products.name: SquadAMP.com
products.summary: An in-development service concept for personalized athlete and team anthems, shaped through a proposed AI-assisted music workflow.
products.problem: Athletes and teams want distinctive entrance music without commissioning a traditional studio production for every player or roster.
products.audience: Individual athletes, teams, families, and sports programs.
products.role: Service concept, product scope, offer direction, and fulfillment workflow.
decisions: Athlete and team-specific intake
AI-assisted music production
Offer concepts for individual and team packages
proof: The product direction and proposed offerings are documented.
limitations: Public site access, checkout, payment, and fulfillment are not currently verified.
No production link is published until verification.

products.name: AtomLang Evolved SDK
products.summary: Research-stage machine-native messaging protocol and SDK exploring typed intent, content-addressed payload references, and replayable coordination between AI systems.
products.problem: Agent control flows need explicit message structure and reliable references to larger artifacts, rather than ambiguous free-form instructions alone.
products.audience: Developers and researchers exploring agent coordination and typed machine messages.
products.role: Research direction, protocol design, SDK experimentation, and verification strategy.
decisions: Typed packets with explicit intent
Content-addressed artifact references
Encoding, decoding, replay, and checkpoint experiments
proof: A Rust-first research workspace, CLI, and experimental tooling were previously reported.
limitations: It is not a standard and has no universal performance claim.
Benchmark results require reproducible public methodology.

products.name: RAEYL
products.summary: An in-development website ownership wallet that brings hosting, billing, domains, CMS, access, and handoff details into one clear dashboard.
products.problem: After launch, domain, hosting, CMS, billing, credentials, and support contacts can sit in separate accounts, leaving owners without a clear view of what they control.
products.audience: Business owners taking over a website, and the developers or agencies preparing its handoff.
products.role: Product concept, ownership workflow design, developer-to-owner handoff, and integrations direction.
decisions: One wallet per website, connecting providers and ownership details
Developer setup followed by a clear owner invite and handoff
Owner-facing views for provider costs, access, renewals, and alerts
proof: The public RAEYL site describes an ownership wallet that collects hosting, billing, domains, CMS, access, and handoff information.
Its product preview presents a site dashboard with provider, cost, renewal, and alert views.
limitations: The public page is a product presentation; live provider integrations, customer use, and dashboard operations are not independently verified.

products.name: RealBall26
products.summary: A Windows C++ prototype for half-court 1v1 basketball, exploring responsive ball handling, shooting physics, AI opponents, and player customization.
products.problem: Create responsive half-court basketball with believable interaction between players and the ball.
products.audience: Basketball game players and simulation-focused sports fans.
products.role: Game concept, product specification, game-feel requirements, iterative engineering, and system verification.
decisions: Reported foundation: native Windows C++20 / Direct3D11
Reported prototype systems: physics-based ball handling and shooting
Reported AI opponent, animation rig, and customization work
proof: A playable half-court 1v1 prototype and 120 Hz simulation were previously reported.
limitations: No public build or authentic gameplay capture was supplied for this site.
It is not released, not on Steam, and not presented as a live product.

products.name: Throwful
products.summary: A fundraiser management product concept that brings event pages, seller links, orders, payment status, helper roles, and pickup coordination into one place.
products.problem: School, team, and community fundraisers can leave organizers piecing together orders, seller progress, payment confirmations, food counts, and pickup plans from scattered messages and spreadsheets.
products.audience: Schools, sports teams, clubs, and community groups running short-term fundraisers, along with their organizers, sellers, helpers, and buyers.
products.role: Product direction, fundraiser workflow design, and organizer-facing experience.
decisions: One event page for items, buyer details, and pickup information
Seller-specific links to attribute distributed sales
A shared event view for orders, item counts, helpers, and fulfillment status
proof: The public site presents a fundraiser workflow spanning event setup, seller links, buyer ordering, order tracking, helper roles, and pickup status.
Its sample Little League BBQ + Raffle dashboard illustrates seller progress, food counts, and pickup updates.
limitations: Names and counts in the dashboard are illustrative sample content, not verified event results.
The public product site is reachable; live account behavior, payment processing, and production operations have not been validated.
